messages:
maya: FYI hitting OOMs on canary when loading 70B safetensors with current shard layout + warmup. Looks like prefetch is pulling whole shard pages instead of tensor-level chunks.

sam: repro steps?

maya: repro: deploy canary -> send 1 request -> warmup tries to mmap shard A and pulls 2.5GB into RAM, OOM on 16GB host. log:
```
Warmup: open shard-003.safetensors
Read range: 0-2684354560 (2.5GB)
evict: unable to free
OOM
```

joel: hm. This matches the index-first hotstart path we've seen. Some transports still do file-level read-ahead which is terrible for monolithic shards.

rachel: options: 1) embed chunk metadata (offset+len per tensor) in a tiny manifest so warmup can prefetch only needed ranges; 2) force streaming/mmap with read-ahead disabled for large shards; 3) split large shards into micro-shards at ingest time.

sam: tradeoffs: manifest adds metadata/versioning overhead and sync pain for model pushes. Splitting increases bundle count and FD pressure. Disabling read-ahead shifts cost to runtime perf.

maya: thinking: implement a "manifest-lite" produced at ingest that contains per-tensor offset, page-aligned length, and an optional "hotness" hint. Runtime warmup reads manifest and issues ranged reads only for tensors likely to be accessed.

joel: can we reuse safetensors header offsets? In many of our bundles we transcode/pack multiple tensors so header offsets are not preserved end-to-end. A manifest preserves that info across transports.

rachel: important: prefetching lots of small ranges can blow up IO and contention with eviction. We should group adjacent ranges and align to filesystem pages. Also throttle concurrency.

maya: spike proposal:
- ingest: manifest-lite producer in pipeline -> emits `model.bin.manifest.jsonl` (signed)
- runtime warmup: read manifest, compute page-aligned ranges, coalesce contiguous ranges, issue ranged GETs with concurrency=8, fall back to current file-level prefetch if no manifest
- metrics: bytes_requested_vs_used, range_count, warmup_latency, eviction_events_during_warmup

sam: SGTM. Also capture bundle hash and manifest_version in metrics so we can correlate regressions.

joel: +1. Add a CI check that ensures manifest producer is idempotent and signed to avoid integrity mismatch.

maya: I'll implement a spike branch and run canary perf tests. cc @rachel for eviction heuristics review.

warmup-bot: spike branch created: https://github.com/redwood/inference/compare/spikes/manifest-lite-prefetch

rachel: quick note: keep manifest optional and signed; old runtimes should ignore unknown manifest_version. Also ensure rolling upgrades keep fallback path.

maya: yep — optional manifest v1, signed, and runtime will tolerate missing/invalid manifests. Thanks all :rocket:
